mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately leading to lower profit margins and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both GDPC1 and HOUST on a month-over-month basis indicates strengthening housing demand, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals rising household savings, which often precedes reduced consumer spending and slower economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
